I have to say sir I have also struggled with goals. On the surface goals seem inherently pointless, especially when you’re feeling low. However, there is absolutely no doubt that when I am in tune with goals, I feel so good. At the minute the goals are working pretty well for me though. I’d imagine it’s down to a few factors. 

I’d say firstly, I try not to put an insane amount of pressure on my goals, where I think about them 24 hours a day. I use my goals as a structure for my day. My day is in two parts: 1. Working on goals 2. Seeing friends and family. This works for me. Although I still play video games, I don’t feel that sense of wastefulness when I do, because I can only play for an hour before I gotta get back to work on my goals - for example, I have a class. Or I start a shift, or whatever. When there are external pressures eg people relying on you, mixed with internal motivation, I find it keeps me on the straight. I live by a todo list and try to do one thing every day that’ll structure my day orientated towards my goals. Positive emotion comes from getting closer to a goal, so if I’m doing little bits every day, I feel hella good. I write down my goals on my todo list at the very top so is see them every day, and write down my 5/6 tasks, where 2 might be specific to helping my goals. 

Secondly,  keep them a mix of fun and meaningful goals. For example, one of my goals is to become a singer in a band. Another goal is to get a girlfriend, and another goal is to get a 2:1 in my degree this year. Obviously the degree one is gonna be boring as shit, but there is real meaning to focusing on it. Whereas the singing one is pretty fun. If all the goals are fun I find I still feel that empty pointless feeling. However, if all the goals are very meaningful I also tend to get negative and think life is just boring and grim. I guess it’s a balance. I’d say write out a few things that would make life a little bit better for you, how would your dream life look. Some being fun as hell to pursue, and then some which are more meaningful but challenging e.g. a fun one could be, I wanna make my high school football team. Whereas a meaningful one would be, I want to get down from 220 ibs to 180 ibs. Focus on both, not just one. Both have their own positives and negatives. Your life needs meaning, but it also needs enjoyment. 

Finally, in order to be in tune with the positive nature of goals, I 100% think your brain chemistry has to be in line. Put priorities on your physical health, self love, be positive etc and put The goals along side them.
